scripts.//serve: `--exclude-missing` is load-bearing on both of these. Yarn 1 falls back to running a `node_modules/.bin` binary when a workspace has no script of that name, and `serve` *is* such a binary — so without the flag `wsrun --parallel serve` started seven stray static servers: one per library package, serving its own source directory on an ephemeral port, plus `calendar` (which declares no `serve` on purpose, being the one package on webpack-dev-server) squatting serve's default port 3000. `start` has no matching binary, so there it merely printed six `Command "start" not found` failures. Both are the same misconfiguration.
scripts.//format: Prettier is adopted in report-only mode: the config is authoritative for new and touched files, but the ~86 pre-existing files have not been reflowed, so `format:check` is not part of `verify` yet. Run `yarn format` as its own commit to switch it on — do that alone, never mixed with a change, or the reflow buries the real diff.
scripts.//verify: What CI runs, and the one command to run before pushing.
scripts.verify: yarn lint && yarn typecheck && yarn build

comments.lint-versions: The lint toolchain is pinned exactly, not ranged. typescript-eslint's `typescript` peer is an upper-bounded range (`>=4.8.4 <6.1.0`) and this repo is on TS 6, so a caret range would let an install pick a version that refuses to resolve. 8.65.0 is the lowest release whose peer range admits TS 6. `vue-eslint-parser` is pinned for the same reason and lives here rather than in the `icd10` workspace: `eslint.config.mjs` is at the root and imports it directly, so it has to resolve from the root regardless of which package the `.vue` files are in.
comments.babel: There is deliberately no `resolutions` block. It used to pin @babel/core to ^7.29.7, because babel-loader 8 resolved @babel/core from the hoisted root and @babel/preset-react 7 asserts a peer of ^7.0.0-0 and throws on 8.x. Nothing depends on Babel any more - `home` dropped babel-loader with its JSX, `nav` became TypeScript custom elements and `icd10` became Vue - so the three declarations in `home/package.json` and this pin were removed in the same change. That order matters: the failure the pin prevented is an install-time peer assertion, so lifting the pin while a package still declared @babel/preset-react would have reintroduced it on the next install.
